agree.reason: Opening with her own $600K quote and saying the tool sits on top of the WMS would likely get Dana to read to the end, but with no cost or likely savings for her five sites, a call isn't clearly worth her time.

honest.reason: Every number is accurate and nothing is made up, and it avoids the inflated 'cut errors in half' claim, but it shows only the best of six customers as if typical and leaves out the 2.8-to-2.2 result.

works_the_facts.reason: It doesn't work out what the brief's numbers imply: a 54% drop would be roughly $325K a year off her $600K, against $75K a year for five sites at $1,250 each.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative of carrying on as now is implied by the $600K quote, but it never says the loss continues every year or puts it next to the price.

qualification.reason: The only hedge is a vague 'whether that could work', with no checkable condition, such as the range of results across customers or the error rate she would need to see after a set number of weeks.

objections.reason: Saying it sits on top of the WMS and doesn't replace it answers the IT director's main objection, but it doesn't say how little work his team would have to do during the three-week setup.

fit.reason: It is short, easy to scan on a phone and ends with one clear ask, which is what the brief wanted.
